entries.summary: News report on President Trump’s Nov. 21, 2026 interview with Kayleigh McEnany on Fox News’s “Saturday in America.” Asked who he would like to see run in 2028, Trump said of the Republican side: “Obviously, JD’s vice president, Marco is right up there. The two of them are doing fantastically. They’re both very, very popular. But you could have some surprises. We have some very capable people.” Asked whether the GOP “should be an open primary with lots of robust debates, or there should be some sort of unity ticket that the party coalesces around,” Trump said “could be either,” then: “There could be some great unity tickets. I’ll tell you what, the unity tickets are fantastic. You save all that money, you use it against the Democrats. I think it could be either.” He also said that “in another few weeks, it’s going to be starting hot and heavy,” and that “we’ll be involved and we’ll be watching.” The article does not record him naming who would be president or vice president on such a ticket, or formally endorsing either man. This is a return to a theme he has raised before: at a May 11, 2026 Rose Garden dinner he called a Vance–Rubio pairing a “dream team” and “a perfect ticket” (Newsweek), and in a June 3, 2026 New York Post “Pod Force One” interview he said, “I like them both, and I like them together,” and “I don’t know how you beat them if they’re together. That would be a great team” (The Hill; Reuters quoted him as saying “I would think that JD and Marco as a team would be very hard to beat”). The @FoxNews post of today’s interview (29.5 million followers; 334 likes, 56 reposts, 79 replies, 11 quotes, 89,015 views at the time of this update) used the same “doing fantastically” line and a 51-second clip.

authenticity.evidence: News report on a televised interview. Quotes were checked against the Fox News article and against clip posts of the same interview on X (including @EricLDaugh and @FoxNews).

entries.audience_sample: The official @FoxNews post of the story (https://x.com/FoxNews/status/2124165345741041956) had modest engagement for a 29.5-million-follower account. Large-account relays are logged as separate entries (Eric Daugherty, Gunther Eagleman, Mario Nawfal). No 50,000-plus-follower critic of Vance was identified in the replies or quotes opened under the main clip post.

entries.summary: Chief content officer at Right Line News and Florida’s Voice (per bio) posted a 67-second clip from Trump’s Fox interview, writing that Trump “just floated a 2028 GOP ‘UNITY TICKET’ and mentioned JD Vance and Marco Rubio when asked who might run.” The on-screen quotes match the Fox write-up: “JD is the vice president. Marco is right up there. The two of them are doing fantastically,” and, asked about an open primary versus “some sort of unity ticket,” “Could be either. There could be some great unity tickets. I’ll tell you what, unity tickets are fantastic. You save all that money, you use it against the Democrats.” Daugherty added that the two are in a “dead heat” at “Vance at 33.3% and Rubio at 32.6% in the national primary polling average,” recalled Trump’s May “dream team” line, and said the field “might just get packed.” Those 33.3 / 32.6 figures are his, not this tracker’s average (this site’s opened-poll average is Vance 33.9 / Rubio 31.6).

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created August 2016 (1,247,543 followers, 2,735 following, 106,271 posts, blue verified). Engagement is modest relative to follower count (0.05%) and like-to-view ratio is about 0.65% (471 likes on 71,978 views), not an inflated pattern. The 25 replies and 20 quote/related posts opened were unique text, with a mix of support for a ticket, preference for an open primary, and skepticism of Vance; no copy-paste flood.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened leaned mixed-to-skeptical of a Vance-led ticket or of skipping a primary (“DeSantis 2028 we want a primary… No more coronations”; “No on JD”; “Not Vance at top of ticket”; some preferred Rubio or a Rubio–DeSantis ticket). A minority backed pairing them. Quote posts were similarly split and low-reach; one small account wrote that “Vance’s strength lies in the Rust Belt while Rubio’s strength lies in the Sun Belt so that would make a strong ticket” (23 likes). No accounts with 50,000 or more followers, or a major-organization tie, were found in the replies or quotes opened, so no one was added to the opposition list. Highest-follower reply opened was @snorman1776 (13,267), asking what evidence there is that Vance is a more effective executive than DeSantis.

entries.summary: Political commentator (per bio) posted a 60-second clip of the same Fox interview, writing that Trump said he was “a little surprised” Kamala Harris is doing well for 2028 “and the whole room laughed,” that Democrats “might end up with somebody nobody’s ever heard of,” and that “On our side, he says JD Vance and Marco Rubio are ‘doing fantastically,’ and he likes the idea of a UNITY TICKET.” Eagleman added: “I love it. We have a deep bench with Vance and Rubio. Meanwhile, their bench is Kamala, AOC and a mystery candidate. 2028 is looking GOOD.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created January 2021 (1,771,010 followers; following 102,174, a follow-back pattern already noted on this account). Engagement is modest (0.01% of followers; 137 likes on 10,476 views), not a suspicious spike, and is actually lighter than this account’s Nov. 20 post on the same topic of Trump and Vance. No copy-paste pattern was visible in the item opened.

entries.audience_sample: The 24 replies were not fully sampled. Engagement is low relative to the account’s 1.77 million followers, consistent with an organic, early-morning clip post rather than coordinated amplification.

entries.summary: Large news-aggregation account (3.99 million followers) wrote that “Trump says a 2028 Republican unity ticket could WORK WELL,” quoting “JD is the vice president. Marco is right up there. The 2 of them are doing fantastically,” and summarizing that Republicans “could either hold an open primary or unite behind one ticket early, saving money to spend against Democrats instead.” The post notes that “Trump has already called a Vance-Rubio ticket a dream team” (the May 2026 Rose Garden remark). Credited to “Writer: Lucas.” Views (32,537) outpaced likes (40), a pattern this account often shows on news posts.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Established mega-account created October 2020 (3,991,953 followers, 51,751 following, 284,261 posts, blue verified). Engagement rate versus followers is extremely low (0.00% at two decimal places), typical for this account’s news posts and not a suspicious spike. The 23 replies versus 40 likes (57.5% reply-to-like) point to conversation rather than quiet amplification.

entries.audience_sample: Replies were not fully sampled. No 50,000-plus-follower critic of Vance was identified among the quote-posts opened from the related Daugherty clip, which Nawfal’s item also circulated.

entries.summary: Quoting Axios's report on a new OnMessage Inc. poll (commissioned by the Combat Antisemitism Movement's political arm) of 1,000 Republican voters in Iowa, New Hampshire, Nevada, and South Carolina, Price wrote, “You’re never going to believe this but it turns out that Vice President Vance and his foreign policy views are very popular with Republican Primary voters.” He attached a screenshot of Axios’s write-up, which this update also opened, stating that Vance was viewed 80% favorably and 19% unfavorably (net +61) among those voters, ahead of President Trump at 75/23 (net +52), and that 59% agreed with a statement Axios said “generally reflects the vice president's position”: “Israel has a right to exist, and America should remain its ally, however criticism of its government is legitimate, but when it turns into antisemitism that is unacceptable.” The poll was conducted Nov. 7–10, 2026 (margin of error ±3.1%). Axios noted that the survey was conducted for an advocacy group and that some of its questions are leading.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created August 2017 (526,350 followers, 3,280 following, 61,532 posts, blue verified). Engagement is modest relative to follower count (0.06%) and like-to-view ratio is about 1.4% (227 likes on 16,355 views), not an inflated pattern. The 27 replies opened were mostly unique text, with a mix of agreement and pushback and no copy-paste flood. A few very new, low-follower accounts appeared in the replies, but they were a small minority and did not drive the engagement.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were mixed and leaned toward skepticism of Price or the poll wording, with a minority backing Vance (e.g., “Vance is wise beyond his 42 years. We hit the jackpot with him”). Several challenged the claim or Vance (“When you strip out all detail from any statement it will poll as unobjectionable”; “The gop voters support Israel.  Vance does not”; “JD has been a big disappointment”; “He could NEVER win the general”). Prominent accounts (50,000+ followers or a major-org tie): Steve Cortes (@SteveCortes, 536,446), already in the tracker as a Vance supporter, quoted the post: “JD Vance’s America First foreign policy of realism and restraint is correct and very popular.” Douglass Mackey (@douglassmackey, 79,629) quoted it to say the surveyed statement was “crafted … as unobjectionable as possible.” Max Abrahms (@MaxAbrahms, 93,122), who describes himself in his bio as an international security professor, replied that Price “sound[ed] exactly like a leftwinger” for highlighting a question about whether “Israel has a right to exist.” None was added to the opposition list: Cortes is supportive, and Mackey and Abrahms were criticizing the poll wording or Price’s framing, not offering a critique of Vance’s record. Bradley Devlin (@bradleydevlin, 17,076) also quoted the post supportively (“Don’t let bad actors gaslight you, folks”) but is below the 50,000-follower threshold.

entries.source: The New York Times (Tyler Pager), syndicated by The Seattle Times
entries.summary: News report. Says Trump first called Vance's post-midterm analysis 'largely true' but has since complained to aides and allies that Vance should have said the decision to go to war with Iran was right, while praising Marco Rubio in private as a possible 2028 candidate (anonymous sources). Notes Trump pulled Vance from Iran peace talks to focus on a fraud investigation, that Vance says there is 'no daylight' with the president and will decide on 2028 'sometime next year,' and that allies say he is genuinely undecided. Quotes Alyssa Farah Griffin, Rob Flaherty and Chris Christie. Widely picked up on X (e.g., @DeItaone, @MarioNawfal, @RpsAgainstTrump, @LeadingReport).

authenticity.evidence: Newspaper report (NYT, syndicated text opened on The Seattle Times). Relies on anonymous sources; Vance's office declined to comment.

entries.audience_sample: Reaction under the most-shared X relays was split. Under @LeadingReport's post (1,010,690 followers; 989 likes, 53,524 views) most replies opened defended Vance ('Vance is 100% correct'; 'Trump reportedly frustrated with JD Vance for telling the truth'). Under @RyanAFournier's relay (separate entry) replies leaned against Vance. Ed Morrissey of Hot Air (@EdMorrissey, 65,144) questioned whether 'the New York Times' sources [are] spinning their own interests.'

entries.summary: Relaying the NYT report, wrote that 'Trump is having a meltdown behind closed doors' over Vance blaming the midterm loss on the Iran war, and that per the NYT 'Trump views Vance as a traitor for refusing to defend his decision to attack Iran' and has 'frozen Vance out.' The opened NYT text does not use the word 'traitor'; it says Trump complained Vance should have defended the decision and that Trump pulled Vance from Iran peace talks.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Blue-check account created April 2023 (bio: 'Constitutional Conservative. Journalist.'). 1,689 likes on 31,941 views is a high like-to-view ratio (about 5.3%), which can reflect a loyal follower base or coordinated liking; reply sample did not show duplicated text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were mixed and mostly low-reach. Some attacked Vance ('Vance is a Palantir product'; 'willing to lie, back stab'), some doubted the NYT ('i don't trust anything the NYT says'), and some saw the distance helping Vance ('Ironically, that distance might help Vance'). Several replies contained antisemitic remarks. No 50K+ or major-organization accounts in the replies or quotes opened; the largest quoter was @Snowball1776 (44,612): 'Vance is the new Pence !!!'

entries.summary: Founder of Students for Trump (per bio) relayed the NYT report: Trump is 'reportedly growing frustrated' with Vance over blaming the Iran war for midterm losses, wanted Vance to defend the strike, and is 'reportedly sidelining Vance.' Relay without added commentary in the opened text.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Account created July 2010. Engagement 0.06% of followers, low rather than inflated; high reply share (27% of likes) indicates real argument in the thread.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened leaned against Vance ('Vance is not ready'; 'Rubio is definitely more Presidential'; 'Vance is a weak fraud'), with a minority pushing back on the NYT or Fournier ('You quote NY Slime like it is a reputable source'; 'JD IS CORRECT'). No 50K+ or major-organization accounts in the replies opened.

If we had to do it again absolutely,' adding: 'Vance STILL has not said this.' In a follow-up (7:06 AM PT) answering Mollie Hemingway, he said 'This is the third time he's said Vance' left that out.

entries.source: Brian Kilmeade (The Brian Kilmeade Show), reported by Mediaite
entries.theme: Iran war / 'forever war' / fitness for office
entries.summary: On his radio show Tuesday, Nov 17, Fox & Friends co-host Brian Kilmeade played Vance's Nov 16 Ingraham Angle answer that whatever Trump decides on Iran, 'there are going to be people who demand more, who want the war to go on indefinitely,' and that Trump 'is not going to let this become a forever war.' Kilmeade called that 'another straw man argument,' said 'there is not one person that I have ever met that wants an endless war,' and said of Vance: 'Never should have been vice president.' He also objected to Vance's post-midterm line that any honest conversation about the losses 'has to start with the Iran war.' Also reported by The Hill, TV Insider, HuffPost and The Daily Beast (opened). Kilmeade did not post the remarks on his own X account in this window; the follower count is his @kilmeade account.

authenticity.evidence: Radio/podcast remarks reported by several outlets (Mediaite, The Hill, TV Insider, HuffPost, Daily Beast pages opened). The most-shared X clip, by Daily Caller's John Loftus (@JohnCFLoftus1, 2,858 followers, account created March 2020), had 267 likes, 65 reposts, 42 replies, 14 quotes and 66,182 views as of this update: far beyond the poster's follower base, which is consistent with organic pickup by larger accounts quoting it rather than a bot push; heuristic only.

entries.audience_sample: Reaction under the Loftus clip and its quotes leaned toward pushing back on Kilmeade, i.e., defending Vance (e.g., 'Kilmeade is an idiot. Trump's war on Iran for Israel lost us the mid terms'), with a minority agreeing ('Kilmeade is correct'). Prominent quoters: former Rep. Barbara Comstock (39,422 followers; former VA-10 congresswoman) — 'So @JDVance bogus straw men arguments annoy everyone?' (74 likes, 7,865 views); Guardian media reporter Jeremy Barr (29,080) — 'one of the strongest critiques I've seen in a while' (reporter's observation, not an endorsement; 33 likes, 5,704 views); The Federalist senior editor John Daniel Davidson (39,716) pushed back on Kilmeade: 'What's aggravating is the idiotic neocon riposte that "no one's calling for a forever war"'; Douglass Mackey (79,635) also pushed back: 'wars can drag on for years once you start them'; @a_newsman (14,542) — 'Murdoch sending out Brian Kilmeade... to sell wars' (140 likes). Steve Cortes's supportive counter-post (separate entry) quoted the clip.

entries.summary: Former Republican Rep. Barbara Comstock (VA-10, per her bio) said Americans are alarmed by the wave of outages 'because we have no adults in this Admin,' calling Vance 'an inexperienced child from a dysfunctional family with no expertise' who 'spends most of his time on podcasts, Fox, and vacations,' and suggested 'serious Senate Republicans may think about staging an intervention.' Below the 50K follower line; included as a former member of Congress. On Nov 18 she also quoted the Kilmeade clip ('So @JDVance bogus straw men arguments annoy everyone?') and reposted an On Point poll showing Ossoff leading Vance 50–37.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created May 2009 with 39,422 followers, 4,527 following and 41,173 posts; bio identifies her as a former VA-10 Representative. Engagement (3.4% of followers, 7.7% of views) is high but consistent with a viral anti-administration post; quotes opened were short endorsements ('This, This, This!!!', 'Amen') from established small accounts plus one repeated multi-post outage thread; no copy-paste flood.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly agreed with her (e.g., 'The administration is clueless'), with some pushback from Trump supporters ('It's happening worldwide'). No 50K+ or major-organization accounts were found among the replies and quotes opened; the largest quote was by a former VOA host (@by_xubo, 26,118 followers) translating the post into Chinese.

No 50K+ or major-organization accounts were found in the replies opened.

entries.summary: Levin attacked what he called 'Vancette isolationists' as 'the most dangerous buffoons of all,' arguing they 'don't even agree with Vance' because Vance has said he supported the June 2025 strike on Iran's nuclear sites and the February operations, and asking what they would do about Iran's missiles and nuclear program. The post targets Vance's backers rather than Vance himself, so it is logged as mixed and is not counted as a new critical item for Levin.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Long-standing official show account (created May 2009; 5,049,065 followers; follows 1). Engagement (0.02% of followers) is modest and in line with his other recent posts in the tracker.

Several replies contained antisemitic remarks from small accounts. The largest replier was the automated @grok account answering side questions; no 50K+ human or major-organization accounts were found.

entries.summary: In a thread asking which elected Republican besides Trump has the most “raw political talent” (charisma and “vibes,” not policy agreement), Walsh surveyed replies and posted a 24-hour poll of the four names that came up most: Vance, Rubio, Gill, and DeSantis. A later reply in the comments identified Gill as Rep. Brandon Gill. Final result (poll closed Nov 18, 2026, 11:13 AM PT; 67,220 votes): Rubio 31,794 (47.3%), DeSantis 19,338 (28.8%), Gill 8,635 (12.8%), Vance 7,453 (11.1%). Vance finished last. Walsh does not endorse or attack Vance in the thread; he includes him as one of the names mentioned. The original question post (8:21 AM PT, Nov 17) had 6,486 likes, 208 reposts, 228 quotes, 5,627 replies, 566 bookmarks and 3,021,996 views at close.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof; X poll votes are anonymous, so votes are judged only indirectly. (1) Vote shares were stable to the end: from the earlier snapshot (59,262 votes) to the close (67,220), the late 7,958 votes split Rubio 49.9%, DeSantis 26.8%, Gill 12.2%, Vance 11.2%, versus 46.9 / 29.0 / 12.9 / 11.1% before; no late surge for any name. The final order also matches a public count of names in the replies (Rubio 1,293, DeSantis 861, Gill 656, Vance 347, from @frontrunnershow, a 2-week-old 435-follower account, so treat as rough). (2) Sampled commenters look like real accounts: 106 unique authors across 101 replies and 23 quote-posts; median account age about 4.7 years for repliers; 3 of 83 repliers had under 10 followers, 2 had default avatars, 2 had digit-string handles, 10 were created in 2026; no copy-paste flood (the most repeated reply was just “Marco Rubio,” 4 times). (3) Traffic toward Rubio was driven by big quote-posts rather than anonymous accounts: Laura Loomer’s quote (“Marco Rubio… not even a contest”) reached 143,535 views, 8,930 likes and 814 reposts, and Pino Americano’s poll quote reached 23,610 views and 121 reposts. Caveat: among 62 sampled reposters of the Pino quote, 16 (26%) average more than 100 posts a day and 7 use default avatars, a pattern typical of high-volume retweet accounts; that is amplification, not evidence of vote stuffing.

entries.audience_sample: Quotes and replies opened leaned toward Rubio or DeSantis rather than Vance; in the sample, Rubio was named in 21 replies, DeSantis 14, Gill 9, Vance 4. Prominent commenters (50K+ followers or major-org tie), as fetched at close: Laura Loomer (@LauraLoomer, 1,935,729 followers; LOOMERED founder) replied “Marco Rubio” (2,403 likes, 39,175 views) and quoted the question: “Marco Rubio. And it’s not even a contest.” (8,930 likes, 814 reposts, 560 replies, 143,535 views) — pro-Rubio over Vance. Tomi Lahren (@TomiLahren, 2,865,491; OutKick/Fox News host) replied she wants someone who “stays true to the values and gets shit done,” naming DeSantis (2,245 likes, 180,478 views) — a preference, not a Vance critique; Walsh replied, “Yeah but that wasn’t my question.” Three Year Letterman (@3YearLetterman, 486,915; satire account) joked “Gerald Ford” (99 likes) — no stance. Kosher (@koshercockney, 183,833) quoted: “Wow. Nobody likes Vance.” (248 likes, 4,007 views) — critical. Pino Americano (@PinoAmericano, 117,273) quoted the poll: “JD Vance is nearly off the stage. Let’s go Rubio!” (1,187 likes, 121 reposts, 23,610 views) — critical. Walsh also posted a follow-up asking for non-politicians who could run in 2028 (1,737 likes, 682,381 views). Reply-to-like ratio on the poll post is 117%.

entries.summary: Former JD Vance supporter says Vance’s “forever wars” talking points on Iran are getting tiring; argues Vance is talking in campaign phrases rather than as a serious thinker, and contrasts him with Marco Rubio.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Seed post from a long-standing verified account (created 2008, 183K followers). Engagement rate 1.06% of followers and 5.6% of views is in line for a mid-size political account, not an out-of-range spike. A sample of 11 original quote-posts showed a mix of agreement and pushback (roughly half supportive of the criticism), from mostly older accounts with custom avatars and modest followings. One newer digit-suffix account appeared in the sample. No copy-paste flood observed in the quotes opened.

entries.audience_sample: Of 11 original quotes opened, about half agreed with the criticism; several pushed back that the public does not want a prolonged Middle East war. Reply-to-like ratio 18%.

Verified pundit account (created 2009, 170K followers). 255K views and a 2.1% engagement rate vs. followers are high but plausible for a controversy post, not an inexplicable spike. A 25-reposter sample included many issue-aligned (pro-Israel) accounts, a mix of older and newer profiles, about 5 default avatars, several name-plus-digits handles, and at least one very new 2026 account with few followers and high posting volume. No identical copy-paste replies were documented in the sample opened. High reply-to-like ratio (28%) and a large opposing quote (Auron MacIntyre, 3,615 likes) indicate substantial pushback, not one-sided amplification.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Verified Blaze host/columnist account (created 2020, 251K followers). 1.4% engagement vs. followers and a low reply-to-like ratio (1.5%) are consistent with an aligned audience. No bot-like spike or copy-paste pattern was observed in the item opened.

Likes (874) and reposts (182) are very high relative to views (6,615): 13% of viewers liked it, far above the 0.5–3% seen on other tracker posts, which can indicate coordinated or purchased engagement; only 9 replies. The 9 replies opened were unique text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were few and hostile to Vance (“Vance is the biggest Dem plant inside Republicans”; “Vance is the biggest fucking loser there is, standing there laughing while Trump made fun of him and Rubio”; “Goodbye”). No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies opened.

entries.summary: Pushing back on reports of a Trump–Vance split, wrote that CNN’s Kaitlan Collins “tried to start a fight between Trump and JD Vance, and it BLEW UP IN HER FACE… Trump’s answer: ‘I DIDN’T SAY THAT.’ He called Vance’s statement ‘very accurate.’ … No drama, no split. Just another failed CNN gotcha.” (Fox News reported the same exchange: Trump said Vance’s statement was “fine,” adding he would strike Iran again.)

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created January 2021 (1,770,991 followers; following 102,174, a follow-back pattern). Engagement is 0.77% of followers and 3.6% of views, high but consistent with this account’s usual reach. The 25 replies and 21 quote posts opened were unique text; most targeted Collins rather than Vance.

entries.audience_sample: Replies and quote posts opened overwhelmingly agreed and attacked Collins and CNN (“The left didn’t waste anytime after the midterms trying to meddle between Trump and Vance trying push a fake rift”; “For everyone that says they aren’t on the same page…”), with a handful defending Collins. No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies or quotes opened.

entries.summary: Founder of Students for Trump (per bio), who posted critical Vance items on Nov 18–20, wrote: “President Trump SHUTS DOWN speculation that he’s upset with JD Vance over his Iran war comments. ‘I didn’t say I was unhappy with it. I thought the statement was fine.’ Trump isn’t fueling the media’s feud narrative. That’s going to disappoint a LOT of people!”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created July 2010 (1,280,148 followers; following 266,156). Engagement is low (0.02% of followers, 1.9% of views). The 5 replies opened were unique text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly agreed (“The media’s specialty is ‘fake palace intrigue’. There is no daylight between the two”; @EagleEyeFlyer, 47,880: “This was critical he cleared that up!”), with one dissent (“Vance is a huge failure”). No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts in the replies opened.

entries.summary: Wrote: “I think it’s fair to say Tulsi Gabbard and JD Vance had serious reservations about a war with Iran. Donald Trump chose to proceed anyway. The decision was his. And it matters. JD Vance speaks to young, working-class Middle America. Tulsi speaks to independents. Ignore both, and you’re ignoring the coalition that won.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created May 2024 (79,440 followers; bio: “Amateur shitposter… CEO of the People’s Poll”). Replies (70) are 63% of likes (112), a contested-post pattern. The 25 replies opened were unique text; one account (@MyNetConsultant, 3,546) posted six replies in sub-threads, a single active user.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly pushed back (“JD Vance is Temu Tucker Carlson. There is no ‘war’ with Iran”; “Vance - who sides with the Anti-Semite Carlson - is NOT an option”; “Destroying nukes versus appeasing a faction for votes”), with some agreeing and many sub-threads arguing over Iran history. No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies opened.

entries.summary: Conservative news network (3,679,264 followers) posted: “RUBIO LEADS EARLY: Secretary of State Marco Rubio holds a substantial lead over Vice President JD Vance in a potential 2028 Republican presidential primary field, according to a new poll.” The post text does not name the pollster; the most recent national GOP primary poll on RealClearPolling is Emerson (Nov 14–16; Rubio 44, Vance 24), already in the tracker. Headline relay by a news outlet, not an editorial.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created February 2009 (business news outlet, 3.68M followers). Interactions (823) are 0.02% of followers and 3.3% of views, normal for an outlet headline. The 25 replies opened were unique text with no repeated phrasing.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly pushed back on Rubio or on the poll rather than on Vance (“Marco ain’t gonna be President”; “He is not fit to be president”; “Wonder what Newsmax polls looked like prior to the midterms”), with a few floating DeSantis–Rubio combinations. Prominent quote post: Derrick Evans (@DerrickEvans4WV, 865,929; bio: former member of the WV House): “I will never vote for Marco Rubio for President.” No other 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies or 9 quotes opened.

entries.summary: Unofficial Trump-commentary account (bio: “Unofficial not affiliated with @realDonaldTrump”) posted: “THIS WEEKS NATIONAL GOP PRESIDENTIAL STRAW POLL: Marco Rubio ran away with this week’s 2028 GOP Presidential Straw Poll on StrawPoll.us, with 48.2% of the vote. That’s more than double JD Vance, who finished a distant second at 19.7%. Thomas Massie took third…” with a 41-second video. An online straw poll is self-selected and not a scientific survey, so it is not used in the poll averages.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created August 2023 (3,007,480 followers, following 24,921). Interactions (212) are only 0.007% of followers and 0.33% of views, very low for the follower count, which can indicate a follow-back or inflated follower base. The 21 replies opened were unique text, several of them only links or emoji.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened leaned pro-Rubio or skeptical of polls (“@SecRubio is going to be the NEXT PRESIDENT”; “Rubio/ DeSantis”; “We know how accurate polls are”; “Interesting early snapshot, though straw polls can shift quickly”), with one asking “No Tucker? No Hegseth?” No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies or 2 quotes opened.

entries.summary: Account whose bio says “CEO of the People’s Poll” posted: “According to the latest People’s Poll, Marco Rubio leads the race to take over the MAGA movement with 57%. Other came in second, Ron DeSantis third, and JD Vance dead last at 7%. The people have spoken.” Eleven minutes later it posted that, per the same poll, “2 out of 3 MAGA Republicans do not trust J.D. Vance” (38 likes). The People’s Poll is the account’s own unscientific online poll and is not used in the averages. The same account posted a supportive Vance item on Nov 20.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created May 2024 (79,445 followers). Interactions (80) are 0.10% of followers and 7.0% of views; the view count is small (1,149). The 6 replies opened from others were unique text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were dismissive of the poll (“Imagine believing this shit lmao”; “It’s still too early”) or disillusioned with MAGA generally (“I jumped ship from maga we were betrayed”). No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies opened; no quote posts.

entries.summary: Posted: “BREAKING: Brazil could freeze the financial assets of JD Vance and Jail him for foreign Election interference. JD Vance could go to jail for a long time.” In a self-reply thread it cites the Washington Post report (Nov 17, 2026) that Brazilian federal police are investigating Rockbridge Network, the donor group Vance co-founded, over alleged illegal foreign intervention in Brazil’s presidential election, and then lays out a hypothetical “full chain that would be required” (House impeachment and Senate removal of Trump and Vance, a new Democratic president, Brazil expanding the probe to name Vance, then extradition). The headline presents a speculative scenario as breaking news; the opened thread says Vance is “currently named only as” (text cut off) in the probe.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created February 2016 (266,923 followers; bio: “FACTS MATTER!”). Likes (204) and reposts (68) are 9.3% of views (2,922), well above the 0.5–3% seen on most tracker posts, which can indicate coordinated or purchased engagement. The 12 replies from others were unique, short text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were split: many cheered (“Can’t wait!”; “Just do it”; “Yes to Brazil”), others called it false (“BS”; “Liars”; “You’re so stupid. LOL”). No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies opened apart from the author’s own thread; 2 quotes not opened.

entries.summary: Israel- and Middle East-focused news account (1,056,943 followers) posted a 27-second clip: “JD VANCE BACK ON THE TRUMP TRACK ON IRAN. Vice President JD Vance signals support for President Trump’s willingness to launch another round of strikes against Iran. ‘The president is the one who makes the decisions. The president has said that he will do it again.’ ‘My job…’” Frames Vance’s Nov 20 briefing answer as alignment with Trump rather than distance. Posted 8:14 AM PT Nov 21, just before the last update, and not captured then.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created July 2016 (1,056,943 followers, following 377). Interactions (748) are 0.07% of followers and 2.4% of views. The 25 replies opened were unique text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly pushed back on Vance’s sincerity (“I don’t believe JD’s lying *ss”; “He has to say that even though I do not believe he means one word”; “Hypocrite”; “I back Marco Rubio for president in 2028”). No 50,000+ or major-organization accounts among the replies or the 1 quote opened.
